issues.detail: Error handling is limited to ErrorBoundary and validation 400s; edge cases such as codemod failures, session expiry, failed migrations, and rollback steps are not covered.

scenarios.name: progressive-enhancement-task-route
scenarios.rationale: Both use loader, Form method=post, an action reading request.formData(), data() with status 400, plain objects, and Route types from ./+types/notes; A is more thorough (redirect, preserved values, noValidate, SSR note), while B is leaner but equally meets the rubric (it returns a plain object on success and covers the CSRF caveat).

scenarios.name: migrate-remix-v2-to-react-router-v7
scenarios.rationale: B covers future flags in detail, package mappings, config files, renames, and json()/defer() replacement, but runs the codemod without `&& npm install` followed by `npm run typecheck && npm run build` as one sequence; A gives the exact codemod and typecheck/build commands and mentions most items but is thinner and its flags advice is generic.

scenarios.name: like-button-fetcher-and-error-boundary
scenarios.rationale: Both use fetcher.Form with formData-derived optimistic state, a thrown 404 Response, and an ErrorBoundary with isRouteErrorResponse; B is slightly more concise with extra notes, while A adds optimistic count and layout guidance, so they are nearly equal.
